findings.title: Guidance and exclusive reliance
findings.claim: The focus's huda is a direction bound to reliance on its giver: 14:12 joins being guided to paths with reliance on Allah, while 73:9 positively names the sole deity as wakil. Together they make the focus's prohibition the negative edge of a positive guided-reliance relation.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries guidance in huda and a trustee role in wakil. In 14:12, guidance to paths is linked to reliance on Allah; in 73:9, exclusive divinity is followed by taking Him as wakil. These wider contacts return through the two focus words and connect the given direction to exclusive reliance.
findings.reader_payoff: The final clause reads as a boundary on whom the guided community entrusts itself to, not only as a ban on an alternative divine label.
findings.containment: The connection to 14:12 is a contextual parallel, not proof of quotation. The target morphology in these connection rows is not supplied. The pronoun in jaʿalnāhu most strongly refers to the Book, while Moses remains grammatically possible; this finding does not settle that antecedent or retain a special joined-writing reading.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run publication is trusted and the connection target surfaces are supplied, but the integration is inferential and the focus wakil B006 identity is marked reframed.

findings.mechanism: The focus's wakil carries the role of one entrusted to undertake and protect a matter. In 17:86, withdrawal of revelation is paired with the absence of any wakil against God; the repeated role contacts the focus's prohibition and limits what trusteeship can guarantee.
findings.reader_payoff: The Book's guidance can be received as a gift held by its source rather than as transferable possession secured by an agent.
findings.containment: 17:86 concerns revelation to the later messenger, while 17:2 names Moses and his Book. The relation is a wider limit on trusteeship, not an identification of the texts or a denial that the Book was given. The legacy source is unbound and target morphology is not supplied.

epistemic.reason: The support is a legacy retrospective, but the packet independently supplies the exact 17:86 connection surface and its return through the focus wakil; the source-held-gift interpretation remains inferential.

findings.title: Substitute protection fails
findings.claim: The focus's wakil prohibition returns in the surah's warnings about other deities and invoked beings: claimed substitutes cannot remove harm, themselves seek their Lord, and cannot guarantee protection in crisis. The closing denial of partner and protecting ally frames delegated reliance as a rival center of ultimate authority.
findings.mechanism: The focus's wakil carries the role of an entrusted protector. The wider sequence forbids another deity, shows invoked beings unable to relieve harm and themselves seeking God, states that no wakil will be found in crisis, and closes by denying any partner or protecting ally. These independent cues return through the focus's wakil role and expose the limits of substitute protection.
findings.reader_payoff: The final trustee prohibition becomes legible as more than an abstract agency rule: it refuses rival protectors whose promised power fails and whose own dependence points back to God.
findings.containment: The HFT nomination itself has no activation anchors; the reading rests on supplied connection surfaces and remains qualified. The closing wali and the focus wakil are different roots and are related thematically, not treated as synonyms. The invoked beings in 17:56–57 are not asserted to be identical to every possible wakil.

epistemic.reason: The HFT summary is unbound, but the exact connection Arabic independently supplies the relevant prohibition, failed protection, and concluding exclusivity; the cross-context synthesis remains inferential.
